sections.title: Executive Verdict
sections.text: Hold — unresolved. Om Galaxy is a real, established precision-mould manufacturer with meaningful engineering know-how, profitable core customers and a large newly financed expansion, not merely an IPO story. Yet technical capability is not enough to establish an investable compounder: three-year comparable sales CAGR is 7.33%, while current earnings depend on working-capital discipline, asset capitalization and successful deployment into a larger factory and a new consumer-products business. Recurring unquantified MSME-interest qualifications and unresolved collateral-return discrepancies are financially material. These keep all numerical rankings excluded even though diagnostic BQS 5.06 and GQS 4.80 can be calculated. IAS is NS, not an imputed average. The signed October GST disclosure adds 1.88 crore cash outflow but does not establish fraud or an adjudicated penalty. Fresh IPO capital improves conditional financeability; it does not close accounting questions. The right next step is evidence-led monitoring, not a buy call from apparent headline P/E.

sections.title: Research Header, Gates and Data Confidence
sections.text: Exact identity: Om Galaxy Limited, ISIN INE2D0Q01027, BSE 544922/OMG, SME. Accounts follow Accounting Standards (AS) under the Companies AS rules, not Ind AS. Research cutoff 20 October 2026; dated secondary market reference 19 October close 87.25, retrieved 22 October. No 21 October quote or later operating result enters the analysis. Investor horizon 20 October 2026–20 October 2031,1826 days/365.25, nominal pre-personal tax 15% hurdle,12%/18% sensitivity. Position 500000 is illustrative, not an allocation recommendation. G1 Conditional, G2 Hold unresolved, G3 Conditional, G4 Conditional. Primary financial and audit evidence has high extraction confidence; current cash, liability size, terminal economics and trading capacity have lower confidence. Source-safe extracts reproduce calculations but cannot newly authenticate an unavailable original exchange payload.

sections.title: Scorecard and Calculation Audit
sections.text: Canonical factors are GOV 4, MOAT 6, REV 4, DUR 6, CAP 5, CASH 5, BAL 5, EXEC 6, EARN 5; R, D, P, L are NS. Exact BQS=0.8+1.2+0.48+0.60+0.60+0.50+0.40+0.48=5.06, displayed 5.1. GQS=1.60+1.20+0.75+0.75+0.50=4.80, displayed 4.8. IAS uses unrounded 5.06 for Q: known contribution 1.265,25% coverage, missing data bound 2.015–8.765; this mathematical range is not a confidence interval or ranking point. No weight is redistributed. Financially material G2 Hold excludes BQS, GQS and IAS rankings despite complete diagnostic quality scores. GOV 4 does not trigger≤3 integrity caps. CAP 5/CASH 5 do not establish persistent weak capital/cash realization, so the GQS 5 ceiling is not activated; it must be reassessed if repeated poor realization becomes evidenced. Moving CAP and CASH each by±1 changes BQS by±0.22 and GQS by±0.25; score precision should not be mistaken for measurement precision.

sections.title: Business Overview
sections.text: The group designs and manufactures customized injection moulds used by pipe/fitting, industrial and automotive customers. Infuse HRS adds hot-runner systems/controllers; OMG Auto Mould serves automotive tooling. Ownership of OMG Auto Mould at 75% and Infuse HRS at 73% means consolidated profit and parent profit differ. Stable subsidiaries make FY23–26 a useful organic comparison. New Wondra cleaning products are an internally developed business using the group’s mould skills, not an acquisition; consumer distribution and brand building are different capabilities from selling tooling. FY26 revenue 124.0014 crore consists of 91.2920 pipe,7.5665 industrial,17.7165 auto,2.6359 HRS and 4.7905 Wondra. Custom design, machining, qualification, delivery and subsequent service can make relationships sticky, but project orders are not annuity subscriptions. Revenue recognition and inventory costs depend on project completion/dispatch and customer terms. A high-weight mould is not necessarily a proportionately high-margin mould; capacity measured in tonnes cannot be treated as uniform commodity volume.

sections.title: Moat / Industry Position
sections.text: The useful competitive advantage is process capability and customer qualification: experienced tooling teams, customized designs, in-house hot runners and long relationships reduce a customer’s incentive to switch merely for a modest price difference. Repeat customers generated 75.6% of core FY26 revenue, but that fell from 98.52%; the defined repeat measure means invoiced in at least two table periods, not perpetual retention. Top 10 customers still contribute 73%. No independently demonstrated blanket price premium, exclusive customer lock-in or dominant market share was found. Vasantha provides sophisticated injection moulds, Mutual Engineering offers tooling services and Shaily has integrated/captive precision mould manufacture; each has different product/customer mix. Their capabilities show why generic engineering branding is not an impregnable moat, and their multiples are not blindly transferred. Wondra has neither a proven consumer franchise nor mature distribution economics. MOAT 6 recognizes useful contestable advantages, not exceptional structural dominance.

sections.title: Revenue Growth & Scale
sections.text: The declared scoring window is FY23–FY26 because a five-year restated comparable series is unavailable. Original FY22 revenue 74.385769 crore is retained for context only; original FY23 intercompany eliminations and later restatements make a mixed five-year CAGR misleading. Comparable group revenue 100.2989→104.5568→112.6612→124.0014 gives 7.327% CAGR, starting REV 4. Excluding new Wondra at the end leaves core 119.2109 and 5.927% CAGR, still 4. Group FY26 growth 10.07% does not establish a sustained four-period acceleration, so adjustment 0. Pipe grew 14.86%, industrial 49.91%, HRS 13.97%, while automotive declined 31.39%; greater automotive tonnage alongside lower revenue warns against simple volume-based pricing assumptions. Export goods 632.55 lakh were lower than 1152.04 lakh FY25. The 94.42 crore August backlog is meaningful, around 76% of annual sales, but without cancellation/aging/execution/advance reconciliation it cannot be counted as certain future cash or a separate moat bonus.

sections.title: Growth Quality & Reinvestment Runway
sections.text: The expansion is specific rather than a generic TAM claim: mould capacity 1146→3160 tonnes, Wondra 450→1100, factory space enlargement and capability for 30 tonne versus 10 tonne moulds. Existing parent utilization was~84%, so additional capacity could serve real demand; new capacity still needs commissioning, qualification and orders. July 2027 commercial production and relocation through July 2028 remain future milestones. The 100.319 crore project was 23.6554 crore spent by 15 July, leaving 76.6636 funded by 74.6636 IPO and 2 internal/debt. The commissioned industry forecast of 8.7% CAGR is not assurance of issuer expansion at twice that rate. Historical normalized NOPAT/operating capital gives 12.47% incremental return over FY23–26 versus an assumed 12–15% capital cost band, with latest increment around 3% as CWIP and Wondra absorb capital. Wondra lost 1.6898 crore on 22.7308 assets. This is mixed reinvestment economics, not demonstrated high-return replication. The model therefore includes slower ramps, maintenance cash, higher working capital and overruns rather than extrapolating prior ROCE. The physical crosscheck limits Wondra base sales to 18 crore and bull to 22 crore by FY32. FY26 revenue 4.7905 crore on 270 tonnes gives about 0.01774 crore per output tonne. At 1100 tonnes, unchanged realization implies 19.52 crore; base 18 fits without price lift. Bull 22 needs an assumed 20% cumulative mix/price improvement and about 94% utilization. Core group capacity is an approximate heterogeneous-tonne check requiring customer qualification and transferability of applications to the new parent plant; it is not a literal uniform ASP. Capacity breaches suppress conditional returns even when cash funds.

sections.title: Management, Governance & Execution
sections.text: The IPO is entirely fresh issuance, not promoter monetization, and related-party loans fell substantially. Directors and entities have disclosed operating transactions; FY26 promoter-related rent 0.5802 crore, labor 0.5831 crore, and total director remuneration 3.633 crore deserve economic comparison rather than an automatic abuse label. Some remuneration is capitalized rather than expensed. Historical missing transfer/corporate records, charge filing failures, demat allotment lapses and voluntary adjudication are real stewardship weaknesses; appointed compliance staff and refilings are favorable but do not equal legal closure. Unit II property registration is unresolved despite payment/stamping/possession. An employee’s labour/SEBI complaint is contested; the company sets out its response, and no adverse finding is inferred. The October GST search likewise requires follow-up, not sensational interpretation. Observable execution includes increased mould output, Wondra launch and factory construction. Automotive value decline and loss-making consumer expansion offset those positives. The largest factory milestones remain a future test, so EXEC 6 is neither a promise of delivery nor a penalty merely for missing guidance.

sections.title: Financial Forensics
sections.text: Main opinions are not a substitute for annexures. FY26 qualifications extend to parent and both subsidiaries for unprovided MSME interest, whose size cannot be quantified from available delay data. Management cites acceptance milestones, differing terms and no supplier claim; statutory exposure remains unresolved. Bank returns differ materially from books: FY26 Q2 net 13.0555 crore; Q4 about 1.3264 crore. Provisional stock, excluded aged receivables and supplier advance netting are explanations, not verified bank-accepted closure. Original FY24/FY25 audit trail inability-to-comment contrasts with FY26 enabled log/no tampering observed on test checks and unmodified IFC. Original/restated PAT differences, self-generated asset capitalization and 0.7272 capitalized borrowing cost are explicitly bridged. Four-year comparable CFO/group PAT 1.145 and latest three-year 1.463 are real positives, but FY26 collection release and payable growth support cash; old 2–3 year receivables 8.5476 crore have no provision. Free cash is 1.5858, not total bank 6.1015;8.2921 total FD s are liened. Tax/statutory/wage/gratuity obligations, operating rent, subsidiary guarantees and current maturities are counted once. These findings support G2 Hold without asserting fraud or actual default.

sections.title: Valuation & Market Expectations
sections.text: The secondary 87.25 quote and 33,878,024 shares imply~295.59 crore market value. Use owner PAT 15.9974, not group PAT 16.6358, for shareholder P/E; current-share FY26 EPS is~4.72, lower than restated weighted EPS 7.20 after fresh IPO share expansion. Historical March debt/cash combined with October post IPO shares is a stale-balance diagnostic only; modeled current EV separately bridges dated IPO receipt, remaining fees, protected earmarks, debt paydown, GST cash and reserve. Bear/base/bull annual and monthly models run only to 20 October 2031. New project depreciation begins at assumed commissioning, maintenance and working capital persist, NCI is a separate terminal claim and rent stays in EBITDA. Ordinary returns/entry prices are NS under G2. Funded conditional outputs are explicitly not investment recommendations; any reserve breach, even before entry, suppresses non-rescue IRR. The bear requires a separately labeled whole-share pre-funded rescue counterfactual, not imaginary negative cash financing. Sensitivities cover growth×multiple, working capital×overrun, reserves×MSME cost, legacy settlement×project overlap, NCI×interest and 12/15/18% hurdles. Reverse roots require bracket crossing, small residual and funding, never an endpoint masquerading as a solution.

sections.title: Bear Case & Permanent-Loss Path
sections.text: A permanent-loss path does not require the core business to disappear. Automotive/pipe customers could defer project orders, qualification and relocation could delay new factory utilization, and Wondra distribution could consume more cash while margins contract. Old receivables may not collect at book value; delayed MSME payments could carry unprovided interest. Inventory/project advances and supplier normalization then absorb operating cash precisely when earmarked IPO cash is committed to eligible capex. The bear model links lower growth/margins, more working capital,20% overrun and six-month delay and breaches an analyst-selected reserve before IPO. That is a stress result, not evidence the company actually defaulted. A rescue illustration pre-funds the worst trough, charges fees, issues whole shares and dilutes holders; it is not an announced transaction and would alter the actual IPO capital structure. Assets and core profits offer recovery potential, but custom tooling and specialized plant may recover less in forced sale, and an illiquid SME market can make a sale impossible at the displayed quote. Fresh IPO capital and two strong collection years are genuine counterevidence to a simple insolvency narrative.

sections.title: 5× / 10× Feasibility
sections.text: At 87.25, undiluted 5×/10× prices are 436.25/872.50. Over the exact five-year horizon this requires roughly 38%/58% annual price appreciation, far above historical organic revenue growth. The embedded feasibility rows solve the operating EBITDA and sales needed at 10× terminal EBITDA and 26% margin, retaining terminal debt, cash reserve and minority claims rather than adding operating property again. These are arithmetic requirements, not price forecasts. The factory could permit significant physical expansion, but a near-threefold capacity increase does not by itself support a 5×/10× share outcome: utilization, product mix, margins, capital turnover, cash collections and consumer distribution must all work. Any rescue or future issuance increases aggregate earnings/value required for the same per-share target. A market premium cannot compensate indefinitely for weak incremental returns or unreconciled accounts. Current evidence supports watching an expansion, not assigning an evidence-backed multibagger designation.

sections.title: Monitoring Plan
sections.text: Reconsider G2 only after quantified MSME delayed-interest calculations/provision or documented resolution across all three entities, plus bank-accepted collateral returns reconciled to audited books. Obtain actual IPO utilization, unrestricted cash/debt/FD lien movement and project cash spent so the historical-to-current funding bridge is verified rather than assumed. Track GST reconciliations/filings and final orders, not just the absence of a current SCN. Review aged 2–3 year debtor collections, supplier aging and self-constructed asset cost/depreciation by business. Check December 2026 structure, March 2027 building, July 2027 commercial production and July 2028 relocation against original dates; require customer qualification/utilization evidence. Monitor Wondra revenue, distribution cost, inventory and contribution profit separately from core moulds. A sustainable improvement in owner EPS and cash after capital deployment matters more than aggregate PAT. Before considering execution, authenticate BSE 20/60 session trades, volumes, spread, circuits and surveillance; no-row observations are not zero-volume days. Escalate on an actual default, scope-limiting audit, unexplained related-party benefit, missed statutory payments or unreconciled debtors; improve the assessment on documented closure rather than repeated promises.

sections.title: Final Classification & Conditional Action
sections.text: Final classification is Hold — unresolved, with diagnostic mixed business quality and incomplete investment attractiveness. Do not include this issuer in numerical quality/growth/investment rankings while the central financial reliability hold persists, and do not label it a compounder. The 15% hurdle is an analytical benchmark, not a promise. The 500000 reference position fits 3 whole lots/4800 shares costing 418800 at the dated secondary quote;4 lots/6400 shares cost 558400. Neither amount is executable capacity without actual BSE liquidity. No ordinary entry price, allocation or trade instruction is supported. A conditional research watchlist is reasonable: core engineering relationships and new capacity are worth monitoring, but qualification/collection/funding evidence must precede any valuation confidence. Audit closure alone would not automatically improve REV or prove high incremental returns; each factor must be updated on its own economic facts.

sections.title: Sources, Assumptions & Open Questions
sections.text: Financial facts primarily use the final prospectus/restated accounts, signed annual audits and notes. FY23 uses the earlier issuer restatement and a transparent cash classification bridge. Original FY22 is contextual, not spuriously comparable. The signed GST letter is primary-authored content obtained through a secondary mirror; official BSE access failed and is disclosed. The price is a dated secondary historical row, not a rolling current quote. Future growth, margins, working capital, depreciation, cash reserve, liability settlement, IPO receipt date, repayment allocation, project overlap, minority claim and terminal multiple are analyst assumptions. The model includes material sensitivities instead of filling unknowns with neutral factors. Actual MSME interest, bank-accepted reconciliation, current unrestricted cash/deployment, project cash scope, future gross liability settlement and real trading capacity remain open. Output reconstruction verifies retained extracts and arithmetic, not new authentication of missing originals. Raw reports containing irrelevant personal identifiers are not redistributed; source URLs/hashes and financial extracts retain provenance. All annual/funding/sensitivity rows accompany the canonical dossier, so conclusions can be challenged quantitatively.

Repeated MSME-interest qualification: company and both subsidiaries do not provide delayed-payment interest and auditor cannot quantify impact due unavailable delay data. Principal 17.097 crore FY26, with 12.0448 crore overdue under 1 yr. No supplier claim is management counterevidence, not a legal accounting waiver.

Full bank-return tables show FY25 Q4 inventory overstatement versusbooks 12.3511 crore; explanation 8.0839 transfer to own fixedassets leaves 4.2672 residual. FY26 Q2 net bank WC overbooks 13.0555; FY26 Q4 net 1.3263–1.3264 crore despite prose no difference/within 10%.

Management explains provisional stock, excluded aged debtors and creditor advances not netted. No bank-accepted corrected submission independently found; this is a reliability hold, not proof of deliberate fraud.

FY26 standalone IFC unmodified; audit trail enabled throughout with no tampering noted on test checks. Original FY24/FY25 auditors could not comment on tampering due transaction volume; FY24 unprovided gratuity was subsequently restated.
FY26 CFS CARO summary says no adverse remarks but lists parent clauses(i), (ii), (vii). SFS reveals bank differences, disputed statutorydues NIL/no defaults, not a blanket clean-forensics finding.

Restated PAT adjusts original figures: FY26 prospectus 15.4809→16.6358, including tax+0.9984, depreciation+0.3271, deferredtax−0.2142 and smaller adjustments. Original signed CFS 15.4679 differs 0.0130 from reconciliation comparator, unresolved.

Self-generated mould assets 8.0839 crore FY25 and 7.5661 FY26; policy capitalizes material/labor/allocated overhead including remuneration/finance. FY26 borrowingcapitalization 0.7272. RPT director remuneration 3.633 vs 2.9537 expensed.
FY24–26 CFO 3.4333/26.7665/35.0335; FY23 source−2.7449, comparable analytical−2.6118 after 0.1331 financing reclassification. Four-year CFO/group PAT 1.145, three-year 1.463.
FY26 collections release 11.9482 crore while payables add 9.0281; inventory absorbs 9.4299 and customer/other liabilities 8.1658. Thus latest conversion is not wholly recurring cash growth.
FY26 receivables 29.9597 include 8.5476 aged 2–3 years and 0.9658 aged 1–2 years, all consideredgood, no provision. Revenue-basis days improve but aging still matters.
Cashbank 6.1015 comprises 1.5858 free cash and 4.5157 liened FD; another 3.7764 longterm FD liened. Groupdebt 37.789 includes 6.7738 current maturities inside STdebt, not extra.

Projectspent 23.6554 through 15 July; remaining 76.6636 funded by 74.6636 IPO+2 internal/debt. Julydebt 41.7869; HDFC 12.9778 drawn against 37.5 sanctioned. Undrawn sanction is not automatically free cash.

GST search 6–12 October 2026; signed 13 October letter confirms 1.88 crore voluntary GST/interest deposit, verification/reconciliation pending, no SCN/interimorder or operations interruption. Not an adjudicated penalty or proof of no future exposure.

Wondra FY26 revenue 4.7905, EBITDA−0.7046, PAT−1.6898 against 22.7308 assets. Core mould/HRS PAT 18.3256 subsidizes expansion; a consumer brand has no demonstrated pricing moat yet.

summary: Hold — unresolved. Om Galaxy is a real, established precision-mould manufacturer with meaningful engineering know-how, profitable core customers and a large newly financed expansion, not merely an IPO story. Yet technical capability is not enough to establish an investable compounder: three-year comparable sales CAGR is 7.33%, while current earnings depend on working-capital discipline, asset capitalization and successful deployment into a larger factory and a new consumer-products business. Recurring unquantified MSME-interest qualifications and unresolved collateral-return discrepancies are financially material. These keep all numerical rankings excluded even though diagnostic BQS 5.06 and GQS 4.80 can be calculated. IAS is NS, not an imputed average. The signed October GST disclosure adds 1.88 crore cash outflow but does not establish fraud or an adjudicated penalty. Fresh IPO capital improves conditional financeability; it does not close accounting questions. The right next step is evidence-led monitoring, not a buy call from apparent headline P/E.
